name: upwell_hooks
doc: A general lifecycle/event hook system.
docs:
A general lifecycle/event **hook** system.

A hook is an `async` method on a component or service, marked `#[hook(Kind)]`, that the
framework calls when an event of `Kind` occurs. `Kind` is a [`HookKind`] type that owns
the hook's *output* (what the method returns) and its *context* (the typed inputs an
invocation carries). Built-in kinds are [`Startup`] and [`Shutdown`]; config reload is a
kind defined in `upwell-config`. The system is deliberately general so user-defined
event kinds can be added the same way.

# Participants and observers

A hook's [`HookRole`] is its authority over the event it was fired for. A
**participant** returns the kind's `Output`, the channel through which it affects the
event's outcome (accept, reject, abort, …), and an error or panic is fail-closed: the
kind's [`ends_event`](HookKind::ends_event) decides whether it ends the event. An
**observer** (`#[hook(Kind, observe)]`) has no say: it returns `()` or `Result<(), E>`,
and its failure is reported but never interpreted. Both may run arbitrary code; the
split is about who decides the outcome, not about who may fail.

Observing is owned by the runtime, never by the firing site: [`HookManager::fire`]
runs participants sequentially in registration order, stops at the first outcome that
ends the event, and only then runs every observer concurrently.
[`HookManager::fire_streamed`] yields the same outcomes as each hook completes, so a
caller can act on independent observer outcomes immediately; the `*_all` variants
ignore the firing site's targeting. An observer therefore
never sees an event a participant can still change, nor one a participant ended. A kind
with no outcome to affect declares
[`ObserversOnly`](HookParticipation::ObserversOnly), making each of its hooks an
observer (e.g. [`Shutdown`]).

Routing is independent of role: a firing site selects the hooks its event targets
(e.g. hooks on affected components), and `#[hook(Kind, always)]` opts a hook out of
that selection so it runs on every event of its kind.

Hooks do **not** receive component dependencies as parameters — those are reached through
`&self` (a hook may also be self-less). A hook's only parameters are the kind's inputs,
each a [`HookParam`] extracted from the kind's context. Hooks are collected per type
(the `{Type}Hooks` distributed slice, exposed via [`ComponentHooks`]) and registered into
a [`HookManager`]; a type with no hooks contributes nothing at runtime.

This crate is generic over the [`ResolverCtx`](upwell_core::ResolverCtx): a hook's
erased [`HookCall`] resolves its receiver through the resolver context, so the hook
layer never names the DI container (which sits above it).

name: ComponentHooks
doc: A component type's own hooks.
docs:
A component type's own hooks.

Implemented for each `#[component]`/`#[service]` by the macro to return that type's
`{Type}Hooks` distributed slice — the slice every `#[hook]` method appends to. The owning
`ComponentDescriptor` stores this as a fn pointer, so the registry reaches a type's hooks
without holding its type.

name: HookCall
signature: pub type HookCall = fn(&'a dyn ResolverCtx + Send + Sync, &'a dyn Any + Send + Sync) -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>
doc: The erased call shape every hook is compiled to: resolve the receiver (if the method takes &self) from the resolver context, extract the kind's params from the erased context, run the method, and box its output. A participant's boxed value is always the kind's Output; an observer's is discarded.
docs:
The erased call shape every hook is compiled to: resolve the receiver (if the method
takes `&self`) from the resolver context, extract the kind's params from the erased
context, run the method, and box its output. A participant's boxed value is always the
kind's `Output`; an observer's is discarded.

The call takes `&dyn ResolverCtx` (not the container itself), so the hook layer stays
below the DI engine. The macro-generated body resolves the receiver through the
component source it fetches from the context.

name: HookKind
doc: A kind of hook: the event a #hook(Kind) method reacts to.
docs:
A kind of hook: the event a `#[hook(Kind)]` method reacts to.

The kind owns the contract: `Output` is what each participant of this kind returns
(the action channel through which a participant affects the event), and `Cx` is the
owned, per-invocation context its parameters are extracted from (e.g. the proposed
config values for a reload). [`ends_event`](Self::ends_event) decides which
participant outcomes end the event, and [`PARTICIPATION`](Self::PARTICIPATION)
decides which [`HookRole`]s its hooks may take.

name: Shutdown
doc: Fired once when the daemon begins a graceful shutdown (the serve/run loop has stopped).
docs:
Fired once when the daemon begins a graceful shutdown (the serve/run loop has stopped).

Shutdown has no outcome a hook could affect, so it is observer-only: every
`#[hook(Shutdown)]` is an observer, all of them run, and their errors are logged while
shutdown proceeds regardless.

name: Startup
doc: Fired once after the daemon is built and before it begins serving.
docs:
Fired once after the daemon is built and before it begins serving.

Participants (`#[hook(Startup)]`) are startup gates: they run sequentially, and an
`Err` from any of them aborts startup, so later gates never run and the daemon does not
begin accepting work. Observers (`#[hook(Startup, observe)]`) run once every gate has
passed, before serving begins; their errors are logged and never abort startup.

name: HookManager
doc: Fires hooks of a kind against the live component instances.
docs:
Fires hooks of a kind against the live component instances.

Built once at application build from every registered component's hook slice (empties
skipped), so it can be seeded as a framework singleton. The resolver context is attached
after the root scope is built (see [`attach`](Self::attach)).

name: attach
signature: pub fn attach(&self, ctx: Weak<dyn ResolverCtx + Send + Sync>)
doc: Attaches the resolver context hook receivers resolve through.
docs:
Attaches the resolver context hook receivers resolve through.

Attaching replaces any previously attached provider, so a second attach retargets
the manager. The manager retains only a weak reference, so a component storing its
own manager cannot create a root-container cycle; once the attached context is
dropped, hooks report
[`Error::ResolverUnavailable`](crate::Error::ResolverUnavailable) instead of
resolving.

Upwell's runtime never retargets: each runtime generation builds a fresh
generation-local manager and attaches it once to the root scope that seeded it,
so a manager stays bound to its own generation's root.

name: fire
signature: pub async fn fire<K: HookKind>(&self, cx: &K::Cx, select: impl Fn(&HookDescriptor) -> bool) -> FiredHooks<K>
doc: Fires an event of kind K against cx and collects every outcome.
docs:
Fires an event of kind `K` against `cx` and collects every outcome.

A hook runs when `select` includes it or its routing is
[`Always`](crate::HookRouting::Always). Participants run first, sequentially in
registration order, and the first outcome for which [`HookKind::ends_event`] holds
ends the event: no later participant and no observer runs. Otherwise every
selected observer then runs concurrently, after the event has settled, and its
failure is only reported. Observers are collected back into registration order.
Panics are isolated into redacted [`Error::Panicked`](crate::Error::Panicked)
outcomes. Returns empty outcomes (no work) when nothing listens.

doc: Fires an event of kind K against every registered hook of that kind, ignoring targeting, and collects every outcome. See fire.

name: fire_streamed
signature: pub fn fire_streamed<'a, K: HookKind>(self: &'a Self, cx: &'a K::Cx, select: impl Fn(&HookDescriptor) -> bool) -> impl Stream + 'a
doc: Fires an event of kind K against cx and yields each outcome as soon as its hook completes.
docs:
Fires an event of kind `K` against `cx` and yields each outcome as soon as its
hook completes.

Selection, ordering, and the participant/observer split are those of
[`fire`](Self::fire): participants are yielded one at a time in registration
order, the stream ends after a participant that ends the event, and otherwise
every observer starts concurrently and is yielded in completion order. Dropping
the stream cancels the event: hooks that have not started yet never run.
